meta.title: Hungarian B1 Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1000 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Hungarian → English (see the Hungarian, recall the meaning) and English → Hungarian (see an English meaning, recall the Hungarian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1000 words of Hungarian for an intermediate learner, aligned to B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.' — a learner here is able to deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling, to produce simple connected text on familiar topics, and to describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions, and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Hungarian has examinations at these levels, but no graded word list for any of them was found published, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 426 of the 1000 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — work, money and the economy, education, the news, media and technology, government, law and society, the environment and the weather, health and medicine, travel and transport, the household and its chores, relationships and the stages of life, feelings and character, religion and festivals, ideas, reasons and plans, the connectors that join sentences, words for describing, and the verbs of thinking, deciding, arguing and changing — and the other 574 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Hungarian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case of a noun and every form of a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Verbs are given as Hungarian dictionaries give them, in the third person singular (eszik "eats", lát "sees"), the form the endings are built on. The 448 nouns show their plural, their accusative and their "his, her" form, the part vowel harmony makes hard to guess (ló, lovak, lovat, lova), and behind the All forms fold every case in both numbers; the 234 verbs show their "I" form, their past and their infinitive (eszik, eszem, evett, enni), and behind the fold the present in both conjugations — the definite one is used when the object is definite (látok egy házat, "I see a house"; látom a házat, "I see the house") — the past, the conditional and the imperative by person. The Hungarian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and their sounds. Real example sentences come with 983 of the 1000 words, three apiece for 937 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
